props.title: Made of Honor

sections.content: Made of Honor (2008) follows the well-worn path of friends-to-lovers romantic comedies, echoing My Best Friend's Wedding (1997) with a gender-swapped premise. Patrick Dempsey plays Tom, a serial dater asked to be his best friend Hannah's maid of honor, only to realize he's in love with her. The film rides the wave of mid-2000s romantic comedies like 27 Dresses (2008) and Sweet Home Alabama (2002), capitalizing on Dempsey's "McDreamy" Grey's Anatomy fame.

sections.content: The Scotland-set portions of Made of Honor tap into a trend of American romantic comedies using European settings for added charm, similar to Leap Year (2010) in Ireland and Letters to Juliet (2010) in Italy. This formula combines fish-out-of-water comedy with romantic escapism, though often at the expense of authentic cultural representation. The film's wedding planning sequences mirror those in The Wedding Planner (2001) and Wedding Date (2005), highlighting the genre's fascination with matrimonial chaos.

While Made of Honor received mixed reviews, it demonstrates how romantic comedies of the 2000s relied heavily on established stars and familiar tropes. The chemistry-driven approach mirrors successful entries like Two Weeks Notice (2002) and How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days (2003), where charismatic leads elevate predictable plotting. The film's exploration of male-female friendship dynamics, though less nuanced, follows the path set by classics like When Harry Met Sally (1989). sections.content: The late 2000s saw a surge in wedding-themed romantic comedies, with Made of Honor joining films like 27 Dresses (2008), Bride & Prejudice (2004), and Wedding Crashers (2005). These films often explored changing gender roles and relationship expectations, though frequently falling back on conventional romantic comedy resolutions. The genre's fascination with weddings reflects both commercial appeal and societal anxiety about marriage traditions in modern contexts.
